The top box is the session that most recently went live — when New York's core session starts while London is still open, it takes the top spot and reads "Overlap with London"; once London closes it becomes "Core — solo, no overlap". Before that, New York shows "Pre-market" and London stays on top. After the 16:00 ET close it shows "Post-market". The overlap box below counts times when exchanges from two different regions are open at once. On weekends the same session times and overlaps still run — they are just labelled Weekend, because cash markets are shut. Each box also lists its exchanges (ASX and Tokyo, LSE and Xetra, NYSE/Nasdaq) with open hours, Tokyo's lunch break and when they run together. Crypto trades 24/7, but flows and volatility still tend to follow these cash-market sessions.

Liquidations per hour — last 24h

Real liquidations captured from Binance (all coins) and Bybit (BTC & ETH) public feeds.

Timeframe

Each horizontal band is a price level where modelled leveraged positions would be liquidated; brighter = more notional at risk. Bands fade as price trades through them. This is TTM's estimate, built from open-interest changes, 5-minute candles and an assumed leverage mix (10x/25x/50x/100x) — like CoinGlass's heatmap it is a model, not a record of real positions.

Bars show estimated liquidation notional at each price level, split by leverage tier. The red curve accumulates longs that would be liquidated as price falls; the green curve accumulates shorts as price rises. Modelled from open-interest changes, counting only positions opened inside the timeframe you pick (longer timeframes include more positions) — an estimate, not real position data.

FOMO Finder

Is the market panicking or getting greedy?

A live gauge built from how far perpetual futures trade above or below spot (the premium) and the 8-hour funding rate. Futures at a discount with low funding reads as fear; a rich premium with high funding reads as greed.

Risk Tools

Risk-to-Reward Calculator

Plan the trade before you place it. Enter your entry, stop-loss and up to three take-profit targets, set your account size and the percentage you are willing to lose, and the calculator sizes the position from your risk, then shows margin, leverage impact, estimated liquidation, break-even win rate and fees. Prices are manual, with a button to pull the live price. Everything stays in your own browser.

1. Trade setup

2. Risk management

Trade summary

Leverage impact

Leverage changes the margin you lock up and how close liquidation sits; it does not change the dollar loss at your stop, because the position is sized from your risk. Liquidation is an estimate for an isolated position and varies by exchange, contract and margin mode.

Trade visualisation

Take-profit breakdown

Key risk notes

  • Leverage increases both potential gains and losses, and liquidation can happen before your stop-loss is reached if the stop is too wide for the leverage.
  • Actual fills can differ from planned prices because of volatility, slippage and funding or fees.
  • Break-even win rate is the share of trades you must win, at this R:R, just to cover losses (before fees on a series of trades).
  • This tool gives estimates for education and planning, not financial advice or a trade signal.

Saved setups

Setups are stored in this browser only, so other members cannot see them. They are lost if you clear site data or change device, so use Export to keep a copy.

Volume Heatmap

Where trading volume is surging or drying up

Relative volume compares the latest candle's volume with the average of the previous 20 candles on the same timeframe, so 3.0× means three times normal. Zones: Surging (3×+), High (1.5–3×), Normal (0.7–1.5×), Low (0.4–0.7×) and Dry (below 0.4×). Green tiles with ▲ are positive volume (the latest candle closed higher) and red tiles with ▼ are negative volume (it closed lower); the darker the colour, the heavier the volume. Hover a tile for the candle's move and the coin's 24h USDT volume. Filter by type, search a coin, or switch to the table to compare every timeframe.

Loading volume…

▲ Positive volume (latest candle closed up)▼ Negative volume (closed down)Darker = heavier volume (Surging 3×+, High 1.5–3×, Normal 0.7–1.5×, Low 0.4–0.7×, Dry <0.4×)
Loading…

Volume is OKX spot USDT volume, refreshed about every 10 minutes. The newest candle is still forming, so a young candle can read low early on. Positive or negative means the latest candle closed up or down, not a split of buyers and sellers. Heavy volume on a down candle is not necessarily more selling than buying. Not financial advice.

RSI Heatmap

Which coins are overbought or oversold

The 14-period RSI for the top ~125 coins across seven timeframes, from 15 minutes up to one week. Coins fall into five zones: Overbought (70+), Strong (60–70), Neutral (40–60), Weak (30–40) and Oversold (30 or below). Pick a timeframe to filter the tiles or the table (bigger tiles are bigger coins), or use the table to compare every timeframe and sort by any column.
